1.1: 1.1 Argument. Jude the apostle so instructs the brethren about the corrupters of the way of truth as to argue that it is unlawful for those once delivered from under the yoke of servitude to again give their labor to servile duties. To the comforted and called. Jesus our Lord calls, preserves, loves, and makes the children and members of God.
1.2: 1.2 Mercy to you. If God has begun to have mercy on you by pardoning offenses, may he fulfill mercy, leading by ample goods to eternal ones. If he has reconciled himself to enemies, may he give eternal peace to those made friends, in which you may differ from him in nothing.
1.3: 1.3 Beloved. I, who wish to provide for your salvation, have had necessity, on account of the false apostles who intrude themselves upon you, to write you admonitions concerning your common salvation, that is concerning the faith which is as much my salvation as yours and of all the faithful, namely the faith which works through love. I say, taking all care to write to you, that is all that pertains to care. I pray for you, I dispute against your seducers, and that you may know I provide for you, I write to you of them: I uncover their wickedness: I show you how you ought to hold faith and love: and since I am so solicitous for you, you ought to receive my admonition.
1.4: 1.4 Turning the grace. The hardness and strictness of the law, which says eye for eye, tooth for tooth, the grace of the Gospel tempers, in which committed crimes are purged by penance and the fruit of alms. But the wicked turn this grace into luxury, who now sin the more freely, the less they see themselves examined for their misdeeds by the harshness of the law.
1.5: 1.5 All things. The secrets of the faith, and you have no need to hear recent things as holier from new masters, that is: You know perfectly all that is to be known of the faith, and therefore there is no need that you hear them. That Jesus. The heretics being confuted, then, to recall those who had believed the wicked and impious, he shows how great is the greatness of the Lord whom they deny, showing that he is the one who led the people of Israel out of Egypt.
1.6: 1.6 And the angels. And truly they are not to be imitated who falsely say that Jesus is not true God but a man begotten of both sexes. For if he spared not the angels sinning, neither will he spare men growing proud. They kept not their principality. So men, who keep not the principality by which through the grace of adoption they were made sons of God. But they left their own habitation, that is the unity of the Church in which they were reborn, or the seats of the heavenly kingdom which they were to receive if they kept the faith, and he will condemn gravely before the judgment and more gravely in the universal judgment. With everlasting chains. That is with pride and impenitent heart. Or the divine sentence which will confine them forever. Or the chain is the desire of the lowest things, bound by which they cannot return to higher.
1.7: 1.7 As Sodom. He had given an example of the damnation of those who deny the only Ruler: having recalled the destruction of the unbelieving people or of the angels exalting themselves against God, he gives also an example of the punishment of those who turn the Lord's grace into luxury, recalling the burning of Sodom.
1.8: 1.8 And they despise dominion. In lesser sins, blaspheming majesty: in criminal ones, by refusing to confess humbly and do penance: having no fear nor faith in the coming judge.
1.9: 1.9 When Michael, etc. That is when Moses, who was set as God to Pharaoh, and who was prince and messenger as to others, disputing with Pharaoh, contended, that is made alternate signs against the signs of the magicians, about the body of Moses, that is the people of Israel, that he should let them sacrifice to their God, he did not dare to bring a judgment of blasphemy of this world, but said: The Lord command you. Or otherwise: When the Lord Jesus contended with Pilate, about the body of Moses, that is about the Church, he would not bring any blasphemy, but as a sheep led to the slaughter.
1.11: 1.11 Woe to them, etc. Because in all things the heretics have been shown to have fallen from the word of truth, he shows them subject to diverse evils. BEDE. They go in the way of Cain who out of envy, etc., down to they impugn the truth they have known.
1.12: 1.12 Spots. Not only in carnal feastings and drunkenness do they perish and are stained, but they are also spots of those, and destroy others with themselves, turning the grace of the Lord into luxury. Clouds. He compares himself to the preachers raining justice, flashing by miracles, but the heretics are clouds darkening the sun, setting their mouth in heaven, teaching perverse things proudly, without the water of wisdom. Trees. The impious and false apostles compare themselves to trees bearing good fruit, but are autumn trees: for they bear good fruit late as a tree planted in autumn, either because then leaves and fruit fall, or if fruit grows over, it is adulterate and useless. For if the wicked do anything that seems good, they do not do it with good intention, but to root out the goods that are in others. Twice dead. BEDE. Once dies that which bears no fruit, etc., down to in which the saints are said to be rooted.
1.13: 1.13 Stars. In this he signifies apostates, because in the likeness of the devil they fell from the seats of the angels, for whom darkness is reserved on account of apostasy. Stars. They promise the light of truth in this sea of vices, but never persevere in the same state of teaching or life, and are to others a cause of shipwreck, and for themselves, for the darkness which they brought into the Church of God, the darkness of hell is prepared, and they who troubled the peace of faith by the worldly tempest shall be struck by the storm of torments.
1.14: 1.14 Prophesied. Not only, he says, by my authority do I prove that they are to be punished, but also by the authority of Enoch, that long ago wicked men were foreordained to such judgment, who in our times have crept in to subvert the faith of the pious. Enoch. In the line of Cain, Enoch, which is interpreted dedication, is the first born; but in the progeny of the elect, Enoch is remembered as the seventh, because the reprobate in this life, which is first, dedicate themselves by building themselves up: but the elect await the dedication of their building at the end of time, that is in the seventh. Behold the Lord comes. BEDE. True is the sentence that the Lord will convict the wicked, and of the works, etc., down to for it is lawful to take testimony of truth even from the apocrypha.
1.16: 1.16 These are. If anything good befalls the brethren, they murmur and complain, as if their own felicity were diminished by their prosperity. For the covetous (to whom nothing suffices) envy even from others.
1.19: 1.19 Having not the Spirit. Because they have not the Holy Spirit (by whom the Church is gathered and made spiritual), therefore they are animal, ignorant, improvident, therefore they flow away, because they have not the curd of charity.
1.20: 1.20 Building yourselves up, etc. Building yourselves up in good works upon the foundation of faith, that you may be placed as living stones in the house of God. Praying in the Holy Ghost. That you may not presume on your own strength, but hope in the help of divine protection, not thinking you are saved by yourselves, but ask the coming of the Holy Spirit upon you, inspired by whom you may pray more ardently lest with those who have not the Spirit you be separated from the Church.
1.23: 1.23 And others save. Those who are not condemned with God, but also fall near into the fire, teach to free themselves. In fear. BEDE. This is to be joined to all those foregoing. For, etc., down to lest perhaps he be more severe than is just, or more pious. Hating. We ought not to hate our body, but that it be stained, that we may render it unstained, that from carnal it be made spiritual. Which is to be accomplished not by the power of our judgment but by the grace of God.
